extraction.name: LongVid
extraction.description: LongVid is a large-scale long video instruction-tuning dataset comprising 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering (QA) pairs across five different task types (video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting), built from diverse sources including Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-Vila, and MiraData.
extraction.creator: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, Limin Wang (Shanghai AI Laboratory, Nanjing University, Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology CAS, Shanghai Innovation Institute)
extraction.rai:dataCollection: LongVid was built by leveraging existing datasets including Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-Vila, and MiraData. Dense event labels were generated for each long video using existing high-quality short video captions and filtering consecutive segments that can be regrouped into long video sequences. QA pairs were constructed based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Existing datasets: Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-Vila, and MiraData, encompassing movies, egocentric videos, news, interviews, how-to videos, and other in-the-wild long-duration videos.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Consecutive segments from source datasets were filtered and regrouped into long video sequences. Event labels with timestamps were constructed from captions. For datasets with high-quality event-level annotations (HT-Step for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D), these were used directly; for others, major events were extracted from captions using an LLM.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Dense event labels were generated for each long video using existing high-quality short video captions. QA pairs were constructed based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps of short video segments, categorized into five tasks: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: LLM (used to extract major events from captions); Panda-70M captions for HD-VILA; CosMo captions for HowTo100M; Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D; MiraData original captions
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training: used for multi-stage short-to-long learning of video MLLMs, specifically for long video instruction tuning in Stage 3 (Joint Short & Long Video Instruction Tuning).

name.evidence: we introduce a multi-stage short-to-long learning scheme, a large-scale dataset of real-world long videos named LongVid

description.evidence: It comprises 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering (QA) pairs across five different task types, supporting models to handle diverse long video scenarios.

inLanguage.evidence: we construct LongVid, a dataset that contains 300,000 hours of videos and 2 billion words of textual annotations

rai:dataCollection.evidence: To build LongVid, we leverages the rich diversity of existing datasets, including Ego4D, HowTo100M, HDVila, and MiraData, encompassing a wide range of video types: movies, egocentric videos, news, interviews, and how-to videos, and other in-the-wild videos of long duration.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: we generate dense event labels for each long video. Specifically, we utilize existing high-quality short video captions (Panda-70M for HD-VILA, CosMo for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D, and the original high-quality captions provided in MiraData) and filter the consecutive segments that can be regroup into a long video sequence

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: To build LongVid, we leverages the rich diversity of existing datasets, including Ego4D, HowTo100M, HDVila, and MiraData, encompassing a wide range of video types: movies, egocentric videos, news, interviews, and how-to videos, and other in-the-wild videos of long duration.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: we filter the consecutive segments that can be regroup into a long video sequence, then we construct a sequence of event labels with their corresponding timestamps for every long video based on their captions. In this process, for datasets with high-quality event-level annotations (HT-Step for HowTo100M, Ego4D-HCap for Ego4D), we directly utilize them as the event labels, while for others, we extract the major event from the caption using an LLM.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: we construct several types of long video QA pairs based on the video captions, event labels, and the timestamps of short video segments. They are categorized into five tasks: video captioning, temporal grounding, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: we extract the major event from the caption using an LLM. Finally, we construct several types of long video QA pairs based on the video captions, event labels, and the timestamps of short video segments.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: To enable the model to handle a wide variety of video tasks, we collect 3.5 million instruction fine-tuning samples, including 1.1M images, 1.7M short videos (under 60 seconds), and 0.7M long videos (60 ∼3600 seconds).
